list.item: Persecutory thoughts and poor sleep for about two months: a fixed belief that people are following him and plan to harm him, three to four hours of sleep a night, partial insight; cause under evaluation: active, confirmed [S]
Cocaine use disorder, severe (seven of eleven DSM-5-TR criteria): intranasal cocaine most days for about a year, last use three days before intake: active, confirmed [S]
Raised blood pressure at intake (154/98 mmHg) three days after cocaine use, without a diagnosis of hypertension; home readings planned: active, confirmed [S]

Financial insecurity: years of tax debt from his time as a well-paid athlete, now settled, left him with no savings; irregular income from paid appearances; worry about money keeps him awake: active, confirmed [S]

A nonjudgmental assessment: DSM-5-TR criteria, the DAST-10 and AUDIT-C, and a urine drug test (with fentanyl) done only with his consent and explained as part of care; person-first language; his own goals first. Guideline: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); Treatment for Stimulant Use Disorders (Treatment Improvement Protocol 33, updated 2021) (2021); Unhealthy Drug Use: Screening (2020) [S]

Addiction psychiatry consultation to settle the diagnosis, advise on an antipsychotic and plan treatment for cocaine use disorder. Guideline: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (2020) [S]

Differential diagnosis of the psychotic symptoms: follow their course after the last cocaine use; MoCA now and again when he is well; TSH, vitamin B12, HIV and syphilis tests; brain MRI because the symptoms are new after age 50 in a man with years of head impacts; traumatic encephalopathy syndrome is a research diagnosis with no clinical test, and no such label is given; a structured assessment that guards against the documented bias toward diagnosing schizophrenia in Black men. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (2020); National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome (2021); Racial disparities in psychotic disorder diagnosis: A review of empirical literature (2014) [S]

Safety: a structured safety assessment, a written safety plan, the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline saved in his phone, written criteria for urgent care, and safety review at every visit. Guideline: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026) [S]

Harm reduction: fentanyl can be in cocaine; naloxone nasal spray and fentanyl test strips, never using alone, and the clinic's open door after any use. Guideline: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); Opioid Overdose Reversal Medications (2026) [S]

Cardiovascular risk from cocaine: ECG and creatine kinase today; blood pressure at every visit and a home monitor with twice-daily readings for a week before the four-week visit; call 911 for chest pain, shortness of breath, weakness or tearing pain in the chest or back; beta-blockers avoided while he may still use cocaine. Guideline: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); 2025 AHA/ACC/AANP/AAPA/ABC/ACCP/ACPM/AGS/AMA/ASPC/NMA/PCNA/SGIM Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults (2025) [S]

Money worries: the clinic social worker helps with a budget, benefits he may qualify for as a veteran, and a free review of his tax records by a Low Income Taxpayer Clinic, with the Taxpayer Advocate Service if any federal tax problem is found. Guideline: Low Income Taxpayer Clinics (2026); Taxpayer Advocate Service (2026) [S]

Family involvement only with his consent: he chooses whom, if anyone, to involve and what may be shared; the clinic contacts no one without his permission unless his life is in danger. Guideline: The American Psychiatric Association Practice Guideline for the Treatment of Patients With Schizophrenia (2020) [S]

Sleep: regular hours, no cocaine and little alcohol, light in the morning and a dark room at night; no sleeping pill while he may use cocaine or alcohol. Guideline: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023) [S]
